answer: Written in a short declarative sentences register, it stays short. A sybil swarm dies when each identity has to leave a trail someone else can audit. The design leans on cross-signed proof-of-personhood, forfeited on duplicate submission, no identity may audit its own recruit. The summit holds work receipts rather than names, so the forge of a duplicated claim is visible before it can spread. Only identities that keep producing auditable work arrive at the ridge of payment, so volume alone buys nothing.
